title: 真・女神転生if...

versions.note: the Japanese cartridge (DIGITAL DEVIL STORY X, checksum 0x259E)

sources: The harness alone, from the game's cartridge on bsnes-mercury (docs/first-script.md): no reader's snapshots, no memory written, no play outside the harness. The cartridge and snaps were studied outside it

Shin Megami Tensei II's script doesn't carry: no code of a character drawn stands in work RAM, frame by frame (snaps of every frame over a page typing). What stands is the message window's picture, at 0x7E2900, 24 tiles across, 2 bits a pixel

The font was found in the cartridge with rom-font --find on a picture cut out of that window: 12x12, a glyph to 36 bytes from 0x78001, numbered as Shin Megami Tensei's font (code = glyph + 0x0D); the game draws a glyph's columns 3-14, proportionally
From the font: digits, letters and kana by its order (the fifty sounds), none read by eye; the voiced kana composed with their mark as the game draws it (held against じ and ぼ on screen)
Read in play: 14 signs and 112 kanji, each against the picture of its page; a kanji cut apart by a gap inside it found as the one glyph whose picture begins and ends with the pieces
Played from the fortune-teller's questions through the dream to the classroom and the corridor: one stretch from a state with the script loaded, its pages in three scenes
What the script said agreed with the rows read off 37 of 37 pictures (9, 8 and 20); 1 page said inside a press has no picture. No screen without text was among them

The kanji's readings came from the same pages, so the comparison checks the cutting, the pages and their order more than the kanji; one kanji (願) was added after run 1, and run 1's record of that page made to match: the reader doesn't change play, and run 2 then said the same pages
48 harness calls in all (by the record), none failed; the tools it needed (lib/cells.lua, rom-font --glyphs) are #220
notes: Read by the script games/sfc/SHVC-AMXJ.lua off the message window's pixels: each glyph known by its picture in games/sfc/SHVC-AMXJ.glyphs (the cartridge's font with tables/sfc/SHVC-AMXJ.tbl's characters), a page said once the window stands. Not read: menus and choices, the name entry, fights, the screens before the story; who speaks only where the game writes it into the text. Kanji not met in play come out as U+FFFD and are logged for yomikata unread. Names chosen in play come out as typed.
